title: No structured data anywhere in the sampled pages
evidence: 0 of 10 sampled pages contain JSON-LD, microdata, or RDFa.
why: With no machine-readable markup, an assistant must infer every fact (who the brand is, what it sells, prices, dates) from prose — error-prone and rarely quoted with confidence.
suggested_action: Add schema.org JSON-LD to key templates: Organization + WebSite on the homepage, and the page-appropriate type (Product/Offer, Article, FAQPage, LocalBusiness, BreadcrumbList) elsewhere. This is the highest-leverage discoverability fix.

title: Product-like pages missing Product/Offer schema
evidence: 7 of 10 page(s) (70%) look like product pages (cart/price cues) but have no Product JSON-LD, e.g. https://www.smashingmagazine.com/ebook-bundles/smashing-library/.
why: Without Product/Offer markup an assistant cannot reliably read price, availability, or rating, so the brand is left out of shopping-style answers where those facts are required.
suggested_action: Add Product JSON-LD with name, image, description, brand, and an Offer (price, priceCurrency, availability) to every product page.

title: Article/blog pages missing Article schema
evidence: 1 of 10 page(s) (10%) look like articles but lack Article/BlogPosting JSON-LD, e.g. https://www.smashingmagazine.com/articles/.
why: Without Article markup an assistant cannot reliably attribute the piece to an author or date it, so it is trusted and cited less for topical questions.
suggested_action: Add Article/BlogPosting JSON-LD with headline, author, datePublished, and dateModified so assistants can attribute and date the content.

title: Homepage lacks Organization/WebSite structured data
evidence: Homepage (https://www.smashingmagazine.com/) has no Organization, LocalBusiness, or WebSite JSON-LD; detected types: none.
why: Without an Organization/WebSite node, an assistant has no stable, machine-readable identity for the brand and cannot confidently attribute facts or citations to it.
suggested_action: Add an Organization (or LocalBusiness) node with name, url, logo, and sameAs, plus a WebSite node with name and optional SearchAction. This gives assistants a stable, unambiguous identity for the brand.

title: Pages missing an H1 heading
evidence: 1 of 10 page(s) (10%) have no H1, e.g. https://www.smashingmagazine.com/articles/.
why: The H1 is the primary topic anchor a machine uses to decide what a page is about; without it the page's subject must be guessed from weaker signals.
suggested_action: Add exactly one descriptive H1 per page stating what the page is about in plain words.

title: Slow server response on sampled pages
evidence: 4 of 10 page(s) (40%) took over 3s to return HTML in this run (e.g. https://www.smashingmagazine.com/ebook-bundles/content-strategy-ebook-bundle-3-ebooks/: 47469 ms). Single-sample timing — confirm with a repeat measurement.
why: A slow first byte (TTFB) delays everything downstream, so the page starts rendering late and visitors abandon before it appears.
suggested_action: Investigate TTFB (caching, CDN, server work); confirm the slowness is consistent before prioritizing.

title: Heading hierarchy skips levels
evidence: 10 of 10 page(s) (100%) jump heading levels (e.g. H1→H3 with no H2), e.g. https://www.smashingmagazine.com/.
why: A machine reconstructs a page's outline from heading levels; skipped levels break that nesting, so the relationship between sections is ambiguous.
suggested_action: Nest headings in order (no H1→H3 jumps) so the document outline is unambiguous.

title: Meta descriptions likely to be truncated
evidence: 7 of 10 page(s) (70%) have a meta description longer than 160 characters, e.g. https://www.smashingmagazine.com/ebook-bundles/smashing-library/ (434 chars).
why: Over-long descriptions are cut off, so the most important summary sentence may never be shown or quoted.
suggested_action: Keep meta descriptions under ~160 characters, key fact first.

title: Substantial content offloaded to PDF files
evidence: 3 PDF link(s) found across sampled pages.
why: Scanned or image-only PDFs are frequently unreadable to crawlers, so any key information that lives only inside them cannot be extracted or cited.
suggested_action: Publish the key information as HTML pages (the PDF can remain as a download). Ensure any essential PDFs contain real, selectable text, not scans.

title: Title tags outside the useful length range
evidence: 8 of 10 page(s) (80%) have a <title> shorter than 15 or longer than 65 characters, e.g. https://www.smashingmagazine.com/ (75 chars).
why: Very short titles under-describe the page while very long ones get truncated in results and answers, so the specific topic is lost either way.
suggested_action: Keep titles roughly 15–65 characters and topic-first.
